title: Junior AML/KYC Officer (m/f)
description:
Junior AML/KYC Officer

Company Description

We're a leading Investor Services group offering end-to-end services in administration, accounting, reporting, regulatory and compliance needs of the investment sector worldwide. We employ a global workforce of 6,500+ people across 24 jurisdictions and have assets under administration (AUA) exceeding US$857 billion. We work with 13 of the world's top-15 private equity firms.

Our services are underpinned by a Group-wide commitment to ESG and best-in-class technology including a global data platform and innovative proprietary tools supported by in-house experts.

Above all, what makes us different is our people. Operating as trusted partners to our clients, we deliver intelligent solutions through a combination of technical expertise and strong relationships based on deep client understanding. 

We're driven by our Group purpose, to power people and possibilities.

Job Description

What You'll Do:

• You'll conduct AML/KYC reviews and prepare investor files for various entity types, including Individuals, Companies, Trusts, Foundations, and Regulated Entities.
• You'll ensure compliance with internal policies, regulatory requirements, and risk management standards throughout the onboarding process.
• You'll liaise with auditors, AIFMs, depositaries, compliance teams, and management to collect, review, and follow up on KYC documentation.
• You'll perform screening, filing, and verification of KYC records, while managing and responding to queries from internal and external stakeholders.
• You'll build strong client relationships, identify process improvement opportunities, and contribute to an efficient and customer-focused onboarding experience.

What we offer

• Comprehensive remuneration and pension: motivating financial packages based upon market rates for your role and is proportionate to your qualifications, level of experiences and skills profile
• Wellbeing: additional social benefits
• Flexible working: we recognise the value of working flexibly and want to ensure all employees enjoy an excellent work-life blend. As such, we are open to conversations with employees related to setting up flexible working arrangements.

Qualifications

About you:

• You hold a Bachelor's or master's degree in economics, Finance, or a related field, with recent graduation preferred.
• You bring 0-1 year of experience in AML/KYC, compliance, or a related function, a valuable asset to your success in this role.
• You are fluent in English, with proficiency in French or German considered an additional advantage.
• You demonstrate self-motivation and thrive as a collaborative team player who takes ownership of your work.

Additional information

OUR COMMITMENT TO YOU AND THE ENVIRONMENT

Sustainability is integral to our strategy and operations. Our sustainability depends on us building and maintaining long-term relationships with all our stakeholders – including our employees, clients, and local communities – while also reducing our impact on our natural environment.
There is always more we can, and should do, to improve – whether in relation to our people, our clients, our planet, or our governance. Our ongoing success as a business depends on our sustainability and agility in a changing and challenging global landscape. We're committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable and diverse culture for our people, led by our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion steering committee.

Our learning and development programmes and systems (including PowerU and MyCampus) enable us to invest in growing our employees' careers, while our hybrid working approach supports our employees in achieving balance and flexibility while remaining connected to their colleagues. We want to empower our 6,500+ employees - from 94 nationalities, across 24 countries - to each achieve their potential.  Through IQ-EQ Launchpad we support women managers launching their first fund, in an environment where only 15% of all private equity and venture capital firms are gender balanced.

We're committed to growing relationships with our clients and supporting them in achieving their objectives. We understand that our clients' sustainability and success lead to our sustainability and success. We're emotionally invested in our clients right from the beginning.

At BBH, Partnership is more than a form of ownership-it's our approach to business and relationships.  We know that supporting your professional and personal goals is the best way to help our clients and advance our business. BBH is currently recruiting a Depositary Services Senior Representative to join our dynamic Depositary Services team. In this key role you will be responsible for the coordination and performance of tasks relating to the supervision of assets of Real Estate, Private Debt and Private Equity funds. In addition, you will assess, analyze, and monitor risks and control issues for the products and services falling under the scope of the Depositary obligations.  You will have a high level of technical acumen and analytical skills in order to foster a solution orientated and consultative approach to performing our Depositary obligations

Key Responsibilities:

• Gather and review documentation received in relation to recordkeeping and verification of ownership of real assets (real estate, private debt, private equity, fund of funds) and proactively monitor the status and completion of those tasks and follow up to obtain required client documentation
• Build Strong relationships with Clients and have the knowledge and ability to explain the regulatory drivers behind these requirements
• Review and/or execute daily cash flow monitoring activities by gathering information and reviewing exceptions
• Support team in determining appropriate resolutions to new regulatory obligations.
• Monitor, report, define and document critical internal control processes.
• Formulate corrective actions, where applicable, to resolve identified exceptions.
• Coordinate internal and external projects in an efficient and thorough manner.
• Prepare and review documentation for regulators and external auditors
• Support Team on questions from clients, regulators, external auditors and/or BBH internal departments. Communicate clearly with business area contacts as well as other areas of the Bank
• Maintain effective working relationships at relevant levels with other departments
• Escalate within the team significant audit issues, set direction/communicate proposed manner of resolution of audit issues and concerns that have a significant impact
• Develop and maintain peer relationships to share best practices

Qualifications:

1. Education level and/ or experience

• Bachelor's degree in finance, Accounting
• 2 to 4 years' experience working within the alternative funds industry or relevant business line experience
• Proficient Business level German skills are considered as an advantage

2. Knowledge and skills

• Excellent analytical, communication and interpersonal skills with ability to present complex and sensitive issues
• Technical skills in alternatives and regulation
• Good knowledge in European and local regulatory requirements
• Demonstrates Microsoft Office skills (with emphasis placed on Excel proficiency).
• Ability to learn and adapt to new technologies and systems
• Ability to identify, escalate and resolve a problem.
• Ability to communicate professionally through effective verbal and written skills.
• Ability to manage time efficiently and effectively.
• Organizational skills and detail-oriented.
• Ability to work in a team environment.
• Ability to meet deadlines and work under pressure.
• Ability to manage and inspire people

We value diverse experiences. We value diverse experiences and transferrable skillsets. If your career hasn't followed a traditional path, includes alternative experiences, or doesn't meet every qualification or skill listed in the job description, please do go ahead and apply.

About BBH:

Brown Brothers Harriman (BBH) is a premier global financial services firm, known for premium service, specialist expertise, technology solutions and partnership approach to client management. Across Investor Services and Capital Partners, we work with an enviable roster of sophisticated clients who make BBH their first call when they are tackling their hardest challenges. Delivering for our clients and each other energizes us.

We believe that how we do our work is just as important as what we do. We are relentless problem solvers who know our best ideas come from collective debate and development-so we are never possessive about our ideas. Every day we come together as a diverse community of smart and caring people to deliver exceptional service and expert advice-creating success that lasts. No matter where you sit in the organization, everyone is empowered to contribute their ideas. BBHers can pick up the phone and call any colleague, and they are happy to help. Expanding your impact beyond your daily role is part of how we operate as trusted partners to one another.

We believe stability is a competitive advantage, but being stable means having the knowledge, skill, and discipline to evolve, often-pushing the boundaries of innovation.  As a private partnership, every investment we make is in the relationships, technologies, products and development we believe are in the long-term interests of our clients and our people. Our long-tenured leaders are experts in their areas and are actively involved in the day-to day business, taking the time to provide guidance and mentoring to build the next generation of BBHers. Because we know, our success begins with yours.

Go to BBH.com to learn more about our rewards and benefits, philanthropy, approach to sustainability or how we support you to thrive personally, physically and financially.

Job Description

The Transport Manager acts as the operational backbone and system Subject Matter Expert (SME) for outbound transportation execution across the EMENA network at Avery Dennison. Reporting to the Head of Transportation, this role bridges strategic regional transport objectives with daily execution—overseeing both direct customer deliveries and internal site movements.
The position combines technical system ownership (TRAX TMS & QAD ERP), master data governance, order/lead-time investigations, carrier integration management, and operational standardization across all regional manufacturing plants and distribution centers.

Key Responsibilities & Accountabilities

1. Transport System Governance & Network Master Data

• Lead-Time & Schedule Administration: Configure, validate, and maintain transport lead-time matrices per shipping site, destination country, and individual ship-to customer location across EMENA.
• Order Cut-Off & Departure Execution: Establish and maintain order entry cut-off times and daily departure schedules to align plant dispatch capabilities with carrier collection slots.
• Routing & Execution Logic: Maintain and optimize TRAX routing rules, logic parameters, and ship-via assignment rules per ship-to destination.
• Carrier & Partner Onboarding: Manage system setup and integration parameters for new logistics service providers following carrier tender allocation or carrier switches; maintain manual partner addresses as required.
• Documentation & Carrier EDI: Setup specific delivery instructions per ship-to to ensure dynamic printing on Weight-Lists and seamless EDI transmission to carriers; configure specialized invoicing setups (e.g., single weight-list per order rule).
• Network Availability & Calendars: Update and govern site and customer holiday closures to prevent system tendering errors and inaccurate delivery commitments.

2. ERP Integration & Analytical Investigations

• Custom Shipping Setup: Configure specialized shipping requirements in QAD, including the setup of "special pallet packlist" rules per ship-to upon request from Customer Service Representatives (CSRs).
• Lead-Time Root Cause Analysis: Conduct structured investigations into lead-time performance and anomalies (segmented by site, country, and ship-to) to resolve bottlenecks.
• Order Diagnostics: Lead end-to-end technical and operational investigations on delayed or stuck orders to identify system vs. operational execution root causes.

3. Outbound Network Governance & Service Excellence

• Oversee daily outbound freight flows, ensuring compliance with defined SLAs for customer deliveries and inter-site transfers.
• Track and report operational performance metrics (OTIF, OTD, weight-list compliance).
• Serve as the primary regional escalation contact for complex transport system failures, carrier delivery exceptions, and site logistics disruptions.
• Collaborate cross-functionally with Customer Experience (CSR), Manufacturing Operations, Warehouse Logistics, and Carriers.
Please note it's a 24 month contract.

Qualifications

• Education: Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration, or Systems Engineering.
• Experience: 5+ years of operational transportation management or logistics systems experience within a complex, multi-site European/EMENA environment.
• Systems Expertise: Hands-on experience with TRAX TMS and QAD ERP transport modules (or equivalent enterprise TMS/ERP combinations); solid understanding of carrier EDI integrations and weight-list/invoicing documentation.
• Skills: Strong analytical capabilities (root-cause analysis on orders and lead-times), continuous improvement mindset, cross-functional communication.
• Languages: Professional fluency in English; additional European languages (German, French, Dutch, Polish) are an advantage.

Additional Information

• Master's degree or equivalent professional experience in an academic, research, digital, or information-intensive environment

title: Associate professor (promotion track) in Banking Law (m/f)
description:
Language: English (UK)
Location Luxembourg
Country: Luxembourg

Organisation data: Department of Law
Job Number: UOL07790
Contract Type: Academic - Permanent
Schedule Type: Full Time
Work Hours 40.0 Hours per Week

Job (internal): Associate professor
Job Level: Monolevel
Functions: Associate / Assistant Professor
Expertise: Professors
Role Type: Open Position


About us
The University of Luxembourg is an international research university with a distinctly multilingual and interdisciplinary character.
The Faculty of Law, Economics and Finance counts over 2,700 students enrolled across four Bachelor programmes, thirteen Master programmes, doctoral studies as well as several continuing education courses. The Faculty hosts the Doctoral School of Law and the Doctoral School in Economics, Finance and Management.
Teaching and research at the FDEF benefit from the proximity of European institutions, Luxembourg's leading international financial centre, as well as its vibrant business community. Institutional and private sector partnerships, sponsored chairs and a growing network of international partner universities make the FDEF a dynamic academic hub at the heart of Europe.

Your role
The successful candidate will strengthen the Department of Law's research area in Banking, Financial and Commercial Law, which is a cornerstone of the Department's academic profile and a key contributor to the University's reputation. They will pursue research and teaching in this field, focussing on Luxembourg, EU, and comparative transnational perspectives. The position is of particular strategic relevance given the Department's ambition to maintain its leadership in financial law, a domain central to Luxembourg's role as a global financial centre.
The ideal candidate shows potential to:
• Develop an internationally recognized research profile in banking law in a broad sense, e.g., prudential regulation and bank supervision, depositary law, regulation of payments and payment systems, financial technologies, sustainable finance, secured transactions and consumer financial contracts, links to financial markets law
• Publish extensively in top-tier peer-reviewed journals, monographs, or authoritative treatises
• Contribute to interdisciplinary initiatives such as the FutureFinTechNCER and/or collaborate with the Department of Finance in the field of sustainable finance
• Teach in core areas of banking law. The ability to contribute to teaching in related areas of commercial law—such as financial and securities law, company law, insolvency law, the law of commercial contracts and torts - is an asset
• Cover legal frameworks at both EU and Luxembourg levels, adopting a comparative approach that includes neighbouring jurisdictions and other global financial centres
• Engage with Luxembourg and EU regulators (e.g. CSSF, CBL, ECB, ESMA), international organizations, e.g. IOSCO, BIS, FSB, etc., and other stakeholders, e.g. (inter )national law firms, industry and academic associations
• Acquire competitive research funding and establish and lead their own research team
• Show and develop leadership potential
The candidate will join one of Europe's most prominent academic groups in banking and financial law, distinguished by both its intellectual strength and research output. They will actively contribute to the University's “Third Mission” by engaging with Luxembourg and EU financial law, and will be encouraged to develop into a leadership role within the Department. This position offers the opportunity to gain recognition and respect in Luxembourg's legal community, renowned for its emphasis on financial law expertise and its strong integration of academic insight with professional practice. Their doctoral students will benefit from a strong academic environment and excellent career prospects—more than 20 former PhD graduates from the Department have gone on to become professors.

Your profile
• A Bachelor's, Master's, and PhD degree in Law
• Experience and interest in engaging in academic research at the highest level
• Publications in internationally recognized journals, monographs with international publishers or other publications in banking law (or other fields of financial law) indicating potential for excellent research
• Potential and aptitude for teaching and supervising research at the university level
• An excellent academic track record demonstrating both scholarly excellence and leadership potential
• Experience with externally funded research projects and interdisciplinarity is considered to be an asset
• Experience in interdisciplinary research—particularly at the intersection of law, finance, and technology—is a strong asset
The successful candidate must commit to lecturing banking law, as well as related topics in financial and commercial law, at bachelor and master levels.
The successful candidate is also expected to collaborate with internal and external stakeholders, prepare grant applications for external funding and actively engage with other research institutions and industry partners to establish research cooperations in Luxembourg and beyond.
Language requirements:
The University of Luxembourg is set in a multilingual and multicultural context. The person hired on this position must be proficient in English and French. Knowledge of German is considered an advantage. The University actively supports language development among its staff and offers access to language courses to this end.

We offer
• A modern, dynamic university with a personal and inclusive atmosphere. Multilingual and international character. Staff coming from more than 90 countries. Member of The Guild of European Research-Intensive Universities.
• An exceptional research environment, supported by skilled staff and high-quality equipment. Strong links to professional sectors and the Luxembourg labour market. A unique urban campus with excellent infrastructure
• A partner for society and industry. Cooperation with European institutions, innovative companies, the Financial Centre and a wide range of non-academic partners including ministries, local governments, associations, and NGOs
• Attractive salary and benefits packages with excellent opportunities for external funding. Support for career development and mentoring. Services to promote staff well-being and a healthy work-life balance

How to apply
Online application should include:
• Cover letter, to be addressed to the Dean, Katalin Ligeti
• CV, including periods of absence from work such as family-related leave and career breaks
• Statement of future research, teaching and other activities (max 5 pages)
• Short description of the three most important scholarly achievements (max. 2 pages)
• List of publications, research projects acquired, and PhD theses supervised (if applicable)
• List of teaching activities
• Copy of the PhD diploma
• The names, contact information and present position of 3 referees who can, upon request, provide an assessment of the application. Please indicate their relationship to you
All applications will be handled in the strictest confidence. Applications by post or e-mail cannot be considered. We encourage early application. To ensure full consideration, candidates should apply by of 29/04/2026.

• Contract Type: Academic - Permanent. This position is tenured and promotion to Full Professor is possible after 5 years upon positive evaluation
• Work Hours: Full Time 40.0 Hours per Week
• Planned Start Date: 01.09.2026
• Location: Kirchberg Campus

title: PhD CANDIDATE IN SOCIAL CRITERIA DRIVEN ABSOLUTE ENVIRONMENTAL.... (m/f)
employer: Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology - LIST
description:
Fixed term contract | Belvaux | 48 months

Are you passionate about research? So are we! Come and join us

The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a leading Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) that drives innovation for the economy and society in Luxembourg and beyond. With cutting-edge expertise in Natural, Built, Industrial environments, Space, AI, Security and defence technologies. LIST bridges scientific excellence and applied research to design solutions that address real-world challenges and create positive impact.

The Environmental Sustainability Assessment and Circularity (SUSTAIN) Unit conducts cross disciplinary research to support the transition toward a more sustainable, resilient, and healthy society. SUSTAIN combines expertise in environmental sciences, circular economy, risk and safety assessment, and sustainable innovation to address complex challenges related to human and environmental health, climate change, and resource efficiency, developing knowledge, methods, and transferable software for the simulation and comprehensive sustainability assessment of socio-economic systems. Its purpose is to foster sustainable eco-innovation, through products and technologies, as well as support sustainability-oriented policy implementation and behavioural change to promote decarbonisation transitions.

Do you want to know more about LIST? Check our website: https://www.list.lu/

How will you contribute?

The world faces a convergence of crises that are transforming the conditions for human development. Climate instability, ecosystem degradation, and the overuse of natural resources have reached critical levels, while social inequality, political fragmentation, and technological disruption are reshaping societies. Traditional notions of economic competitiveness, centred on growth and productivity, are being redefined to include social resilience, inclusiveness, and ecological integrity. Responding to this “polycrisis” requires new pathways that reconcile prosperity with planetary and social limits. Luxembourg offers a particularly illustrative example of these tensions. The country enjoys one of the highest income levels globally and a dynamic financial and business environment that sustains its reputation for economic success. Yet this prosperity depends strongly on cross-border commuting, which creates mobility challenges and environmental stress. Escalating housing prices have made access to affordable living increasingly difficult, displacing a significant share of the workforce beyond national borders. The reliance on imported energy leaves households and firms vulnerable to external shocks. Although Luxembourg's welfare model and social dialogue remain robust, they are under pressure from rising costs of living, widening inequalities, and growing demands on public services. Environmentally, Luxembourg's footprint per inhabitant ranks among the largest worldwide, driven by high consumption and land-use pressures that push the country beyond sustainable limits.

Meeting these intertwined challenges calls for coordinated transformations that bridge sectors, disciplines, and scales. Economic and social progress must be reframed within the concept of a Safe Operating Space—an area in which human well-being is achieved without breaching environmental boundaries. The objective is to steer innovation, governance, and everyday practices toward forms of competitiveness that are compatible with sustainability, rather than in conflict with it. The Doctoral Training Unit C-SOS (Competitiveness within a Safe Operating Space) is designed to cultivate researchers capable of analysing and fostering such transformations. It brings together an interdisciplinary consortium to train 12 PhD candidates in the assessment and design of inclusive and sustainable development trajectories. The programme equips them with conceptual and methodological tools to connect environmental sustainability, social well-being, and economic dynamics into integrated frameworks for decision-making. Its ambition is to inform socio-economic policies, encourage responsible industrial and technological innovation, and contribute to more equitable and resilient societies. Luxembourg provides an ideal environment for this initiative, combining strong expertise in sustainability science and policy analysis. The DTU is a collaboration between researchers at the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST), the University of Luxembourg (UL) and the Urban Development and Mobility Department at the Luxembourg Institute of Socio-Economic Research (LISER). The consortium also includes the National Statistics Office (STATEC). In this DTU, 12 scientists will train 12 PhD students over six years (from January 2027), each obtaining a PhD from UL's doctoral schools.

As part of the C-SOS Doctoral Training Unit, in this PhD you will integrate concepts from Post-Growth, Sufficiency and Doughnut Economics into the downscaling of planetary boundaries, leveraging good examples of application to territories and cities. Possible research questions include: how to couple ecological limits and social foundation as an interdependent system? How to define social foundation? How to allocate the carrying capacity based on social foundation?.

You will be embedded in the SUSTAIN unit at LIST and enrolled as a doctoral candidate at the University of Luxembourg. You will work closely with a diverse cohort of 12 PhD researchers across the social, economic, and environmental sciences, contributing to a shared research agenda on how Luxembourg can thrive within its fair share of planetary limits

You will be mainly in charge of:
• Conducting a systematic review and critical assessment of existing carrying capacity allocation and planetary boundary downscaling approaches, spanning economic and emission based allocation methods, sufficiency based approaches, and Doughnut Economics frameworks
• Developing a methodological framework for coupling ecological limits and social foundation as an interdependent system, integrating Post-Growth, Sufficiency, and Doughnut Economics concepts into the downscaling of planetary boundaries
• Applying the framework to Luxembourg and comparable small territories under a range of allocation scenarios, drawing on Green Deal technology targets, context specific Decent Living Standards, and provisioning systems, producing environmental ceiling estimates grounded in social foundation thresholds
• Building and maintaining a dynamic system model enabling the testing of individual and combined allocation approaches, valuing social outcome generation per unit of environmental impact across relevant planetary boundary dimensions
• Collaborating with other C-SOS doctoral researchers, in particular those working on social foundation, Quality of Life, and economic systems, to ensure that allocation approaches rest on socially realistic and empirically coherent definitions of social foundation
• Publishing results in peer reviewed journals and presenting at international conferences
• Contributing to C-SOS training activities, workshops, and stakeholder engagement events
Is Your profile described below? Are you our future colleague? Apply now!

Education
• Master's degree (or equivalent) in a quantitative discipline relevant to environmental sustainability, such as: industrial ecology, environmental engineering, environmental or ecological economics or computational social science
• Solid academic grounding in Planetary Boundaries, Doughnut Economics, Post Growth or degrowth literature
• Familiarity with Decent Living Standards and Quality of Life frameworks

Experience and skills

The Unit contributes to national and European research and innovation ecosystems by securing competitive funding and developing collaborative projects with industry.

• Developing safe reprocessing and advanced manufacturing technologies, including additive manufacturing, 3D/4D printing and reactive extrusion, to create new materials and components and manage their end-of-life effectively.

title: PHD IN SPIN PHOTON ENTANGLEMENT GENERATION WITH COLOUR CENTRES IN SILICON CARBIDE (m/f)
employer: Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology - LIST
description:
PHD IN SPIN PHOTON ENTANGLEMENT GENERATION WITH COLOUR CENTRES IN SILICON CARBIDE (m/f)

Temporary contract | 14+22(+12) months | Belval

Are you passionate about research? So are we! Come and join us
The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a Research and Technology Organization (RTO) active in the fields of materials, environment and IT. By transforming scientific knowledge into technologies, smart data and tools, LIST empowers citizens in their choices, public authorities in their decisions and businesses in their strategies.
Do you want to know more about LIST? Check our website: https://www.list.lu/

How will you contribute?
You will be part of the LIST Materials Research and Technology department, where you will carry out your work in the Quantum Materials Group, led by Dr. Florian Kaiser.
Quantum technologies have the potential to revolutionise the world in many aspects. Quantum colour centres in in wide bandgap semiconductors have recently emerged as a promising platform, since they can incorporate quantum systems, which can be scaled up by industrial processing. Along these lines, we have recently shown that individual colour centres can be integrated into silicon carbide nanophotonic waveguides with little-to-no degradation of spin-optical coherences. These finding define the strategy for developing a scalable quantum technology architecture.
Our strategy is to use multiplexed and integrated colour centres for quantum communication tasks. Key here is to generate entanglement between colour centres based on spin-photon entanglement, as well as Hong-Ou-Mandel interference. With this milestone demonstration, we strive to kickstart subsequent developments towards a quantum internet architecture.

The objective of this PhD thesis is to support our work towards optical interference between colour centres, i.e., Hong-Ou-Mandel interference. The initial part of this thesis comprises setting up our new optical cryostat platform, which is based on a combination of standard confocal microscopy, and interferometry. In the second step, you will benefit from our ongoing activities towards quantum photonic silicon carbide chips in which we generate colour centres in fibre-coupled waveguides.
You will determine the ideal pulsed excitation schemes for colour centres, considering spectral, temporal and polarization filtering. Subsequently, you will characterise the photon quality depending on experimental parameters, and implement initial two-photon inteference experiments outside of the cryostat, followed by a fully-on-chip demonstration inside the cryostat. If time permits, this project can be further extended to the generation of entanglement between two colour centre chips located in two different cryostats.

title: Senior PM Consultant – Fund Migration (m/f)
description:
Senior PM Consultant – Fund Migration

We are looking for a Senior Fund Migration Consultant with a strong track record of delivering complex fund migration programmes end to end, from initial scoping through to post-migration stabilisation, across the full spectrum of asset servicing functions.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead end-to-end delivery of complex fund migration programmes, covering initial scoping, planning, execution, conversion, operational readiness, and post-migration stabilisation.
• Act as the primary project contact for clients, fund management companies, custodians, transfer agents, administrators, portfolio managers, brokers, and internal stakeholders, ensuring clear communication, decision-making, and escalation throughout the migration lifecycle.
• Define and maintain detailed project plans, migration roadmaps, wave plans, RAID logs, dependency trackers, runbooks, stakeholder maps, governance materials, and status reporting dashboards.
• Coordinate cross-functional teams across fund administration, transfer agency, custody, middle office, fund accounting, client service, legal, compliance, technology, and operations to deliver against agreed scope, time, cost, and quality objectives.
• Oversee key migration activities including data readiness, data validation, file delivery, reconciliation, operating model design, service model changes, testing, cutover planning, and go-live readiness.
• Chair working groups, steering committees, and governance forums, providing concise updates, recommendations, and decision papers to senior stakeholders.
• Identify, manage, and escalate risks and issues relating to data quality, system functionality, resource availability, client dependencies, regulatory constraints, and project scope.
• Drive standardisation and continuous improvement across migration methodology, documentation, controls, and reusable delivery frameworks.
• Support Client Service Delivery Managers in identifying service model impacts and ensuring changes are captured appropriately in service level agreements and handover documentation.

Requirements

• 5 to 10 years of consulting or project delivery experience within financial services, asset servicing, fund administration, or investment management.
• Demonstrable track record of delivering large and complex fund migration programmes as a consultant, including administrator transitions, fund conversions, launches, mergers, or liquidations.
• Strong understanding of investment funds and asset servicing operating models: fund administration, transfer agency, custody, middle office, fund accounting, and client service processes.
• Proven experience managing migration plans, conversion events, data validation, reconciliations, testing, cutover readiness, and post-implementation stabilisation.
• Excellent stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence, challenge, and build trusted relationships with senior clients, internal partners, and external service providers.
• Strong governance discipline, including experience preparing executive-level status reporting, steering committee materials, RAID logs, project plans, runbooks, and decision papers.
• Ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams, competing priorities, and dependencies while maintaining delivery discipline and attention to detail under pressure.
• Fluent in English, mandatory; French and/or German would be an important advantage.
• Project management certification (PMP, PRINCE2, AgilePM, or equivalent) is a valued plus.

• Plan and manage corporate tax liabilities and VAT payments;
• Supervise the Procurement function covering third party service provider management, risk management, due diligence, contracts, and DORA compliance for ICT service providers;

• Maintain process-driven, auditable, controlled, scalable and automated reporting procedures;
• Manage process documentation including Policies, Procedures, guidelines, and manuals;
• Lead and develop teams of experienced professionals across finance and regulatory reporting functions;
• Support Authorized Management and the Board of Directors on all financial accounting and regulatory reporting matters;
• Participate in new Project implementations and in the adaptation of the organization to evolving regulatory requirements and Nomura Group operating structure;
• Coordinate with the Bank's IT function on system enhancements and new Projects from a financial perspective;
• Manage external and internal audits of the in-scope functions and processes.

• BAC+4/5 in Accounting or related field;
• Minimum 10 years demonstrable robust experience in a relevant senior Financial Accounting/Audit role in the Banking sector in Luxembourg/Europe with tangible exposure to regulatory reporting;
• Proven experience in managing multi-functional teams;

• Business Unit Asset & Wealth Management
• Locations Building C, 6 Route De Treves, Senningerberg, Luxembourg, 2633, LU

Job Description

Join our International Private Bank Treasury team in Luxembourg and help shape balance sheet, profitability, and capital outcomes across a multi-line-of-business environment. You will work with senior stakeholders across the Private Bank and the broader Asset & Wealth Management organization, bringing clarity, rigor, and partnership to decisions that matter.

As a Treasury Vice President at JPMorganChase within the International Private Bank Treasury team in Luxembourg, you will represent Treasury in key business discussions and connect treasury economics to day-to-day decisions. You will provide independent challenge, deliver senior-ready analysis, and help drive consistent pricing, transfer pricing, and balance sheet optimization across the Luxembourg footprint. You will also collaborate with partners across regions, including Technology, and support regulatory engagement with clear, well-structured materials.

Job responsibilities

• Represent International Private Bank Treasury by linking treasury concepts to private banking business needs and decisions within Luxembourg and across the global Asset & Wealth Management organization
• Provide independent challenge and informed judgment on balance sheet usage, profitability, transfer pricing impacts, and capital considerations in business decision-making
• Support loan and deposit pricing activities, ensuring alignment with profitability objectives, market conditions, and applicable constraints
• Help implement asset-liability and capital management strategies to optimize balance sheet structure and associated metrics for Luxembourg and the broader International Private Bank footprint
• Apply and evolve Funds Transfer Pricing methodologies and practices to connect treasury economics to Private Bank pricing and performance measurement
• Deliver analytical insight and succinct, senior-ready communication on treasury and profitability topics for International Private Bank stakeholders
• Collaborate with global stakeholders across regions, balancing priorities and ensuring effective, proactive communication
• Serve as a key point of contact for regulatory and supervisory topics impacting the Luxembourg balance sheet, including preparation of clear messaging and materials for discussions
• Partner with Technology teams to develop and implement projects that strengthen treasury processes, controls, and reporting capabilities

Required qualifications, capabilities and skills

• Min. nine years of experience in treasury and/or finance within a banking environment
• Demonstrated expertise in loan and deposit pricing and the profitability metrics that underpin pricing and balance sheet decisions
• Strong understanding of bank balance sheets, asset-liability management, and capital management, with the ability to translate concepts into business actions
• Strong knowledge of Funds Transfer Pricing concepts and practical application in a banking context
• Proven ability to operate with independence, provide constructive challenge, and communicate credibly with senior stakeholders and regulators
• Strong analytical skills with the ability to simplify and present complex topics clearly
• Advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint skills
• Demonstrated ability to manage multiple stakeholders and deliver across concurrent priorities in a global environment
• Fluency in English

Preferred qualifications, capabilities and skills

• Experience using Python and/or Tableau to enhance analysis and reporting
• Experience using artificial intelligence tools to improve analysis and automate routine tasks, applying appropriate judgment and controls
• Additional language proficiency beyond English
• Experience partnering with Technology teams to drive project development and implementation in treasury and/or finance functions

About Us

J.P. Morgan is a global leader in financial services, providing strategic advice and products to the world's most prominent corporations, governments, wealthy individuals and institutional investors. Our first-class business in a first-class way approach to serving clients drives everything we do. We strive to build trusted, long-term partnerships to help our clients achieve their business objectives.
  
We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. Visit our FAQs for more information about requesting an accommodation.

About the Team

J.P. Morgan Asset & Wealth Management delivers industry-leading investment management and private banking solutions. Asset Management provides individuals, advisors and institutions with strategies and expertise that span the full spectrum of asset classes through our global network of investment professionals. Wealth Management helps individuals, families and foundations take a more intentional approach to their wealth or finances to better define, focus and realize their goals.

Global Finance & Business Management works to strategically manage capital, drive growth and efficiencies, maintain financial reporting and proactively manage risk. By providing information, analysis and recommendations to improve results and drive decisions, teams ensure the company can navigate all types of market conditions while protecting our fortress balance sheet.

title: Private Assets Funds Supervisor (m/f)
description:
Private Assets Funds Supervisor

Permanent contract

At HSBC, we're a trusted international organisation with a global customer base of around 39 million customers worldwide through a network that covers 62 countries and territories. In Europe, our ambition is to become the leading international wholesale bank and we need talent like you to help us meet our ambition. Whether you want a career that could take you to the top or in an exciting new direction—we offer opportunities, support and rewards that will take you further.

The HSBC Group in Luxembourg is a significant employer and operates several businesses including asset management, securities services, private banking and corporate banking.

By joining us, you'll help evolve and grow our securities services business.

What you will do:

Reporting to the Manager – Accounting and Valuation, you will be part of the multinational Fund Administration department of HSBC Continental Europe, Luxembourg Branch and work in a team dedicated to Private Assets and Alternative Funds.

As Fund Administration Accounting Supervisor, you will be responsible for the oversight of NAV Valuations and reporting tasks, ensuring accurate and timely responses to client and third-party queries. You will help maintain and improve service standards, while supporting junior Team Members (Senior Fund Accountants).

In this role, you will:

• Review and sign off NAV in a timely manner.
• Oversee day-to-day client fund accounting matters and execute operations (including payments and investor transactions).
• Assist auditors, internal and external parties with their queries.
• Support Assistant Managers when required, including contributing to ongoing queries and project work.
• Support all aspects of operational delivery in the daily servicing of clients.
• Liaise with clients, Investment Operations, GDS, Auditors, Tax compliance and third parties.
• Monitor deliverables accuracy and timeliness.

You should apply if you have:

• An accounting qualification (BA or equivalent).
• Relevant fund accounting experience, including supervisory responsibilities.
• Strong knowledge of private asset accounting for Real Estate structures.
• Thorough knowledge of Lux GAAP and IFRS, including Consolidation requirement.
• Good understanding of fund structures: pooling/multi-class/feeder/parallel and hybrid funds.
• Experience using accounting software Yardi.
• Understanding of Luxembourg fund regulation.
• Fluency in English (written and spoken); additional languages are an advantage.

Even if you feel you do not meet 100% of our qualifications, we encourage you to apply, if you believe this role is right for you.

What you'll get in return:

The pay range for this role is EUR 68,400 – 83,000.

HSBC operates multiple variable pay plans, to reflect the diverse nature of the businesses, roles and markets in which we operate. Variable pay is designed to reward colleagues for their individual performance and contribution, as well as the performance of their relevant Business / Infrastructure, and the overall Group.

We offer a comprehensive and competitive package of benefits usually covering health support, life assurance, pension, and family friendly leaves, as well as many other benefits to support your wellbeing.

HSBC has been certified “Top Employer 2026” in Europe. This recognition from the Top Employers Institute rewards our HR practices and recognises HSBC as an HR Leader in France, Germany, Italy, Ireland, Luxembourg, The Netherlands, Poland and Spain.

If you're looking for a career where you will be respected as an individual and valued for the contributions you make, please visit our career page, and discover how diversity drives our success.

Being open to different points of view is important for our business and the communities we serve. At HSBC, we're dedicated to creating diverse and inclusive workplaces. We are committed to removing barriers and ensuring careers at HSBC are inclusive and accessible for everyone to be at their best. If you have a need that requires accommodations or changes during the recruitment process, please let us know.

Please note that every selected candidate will have to provide us with a valid criminal record check in due time.

Personal data held by the Bank relating to employment applications will be used in accordance with our Privacy Statement, which is available on our website. For any GDPR request, please send it to: lux.data.privacy@hsbc.com

For further information on building your career at HSBC, please visit: www.hsbc.com/careers

title: Partner & Client Services Senior Officer - Swedish Market (m/f)
description:
Partner & Client Services Senior Officer - Swedish Market
Customer Operations - Findel, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg

About Utmost International

Utmost International is a leading provider of insurance-based wealth solutions operating across the UK, Europe, Latin America, Asia, and the Middle East. Its solutions are largely based on unit-linked insurance policies, serving the needs of affluent, high net worth (HNW), and ultra-high net worth (UHNW) individuals.

About Utmost Luxembourg S.A.

Sitting at the crossroads of private banking, asset management, and insurance, we operate in a well-established and fast-growing division of the financial services industry. Our dynamic international team of 450+ experienced wealth structuring specialists, subject-matter and technical experts consists of 50 different nationalities, speaking over 30 languages.

We are a diverse and inclusive organisation driven by a values-based culture that promotes excellence, ambition, and innovation. We invest in talented teams who develop their expertise, curated through support and training, and fostered through a people centred culture. Our people truly are our greatest asset!

Your role - Are you ready for a challenge?

The Senior Account Officer - Swedish and Norwegian Market is responsible for assisting in the timely and effective day to day processing of servicing activities for Swedish and Norwegian policies. Ensuring that all work items are processed in accordance with compliance obligations and within agreed service standards.
The Account Officer may help the team to support additional/exceptional workload.
The ideal candidate will be flexible in handling daily operations related to servicing existing clients and policyholders along with custodian account processing requirements.

Your responsibilities will be as follows:

The Senior Account Officer - Swedish and Norwegian Market is accountable for:
• Providing daily support to Partners, Clients and Sales colleagues;
• Handling daily workload in an accurate and timely manner meeting, exceeding where possible the Service Standards;
• Accurate and timely processing of policy transactions, servicing and query resolution during the life cycle of a policy, including document management;
• Proactively following up and monitor all transactions and queries received from both internal and external parties;
• Managing risk within your area of responsibility including adherence to Corporate Policy on Compliance and Risk;
• Respecting the planning established by your line manager in relation to business activities;
• Following instructions and process information accurately and in a timely manner;
• Prioritising multiple tasks while remaining calm and positive under pressure;
• Maintaining an on-going awareness of service, propose suggested improvement to your line manager and ensure quality improvements are made, as agreed.

Your profile - Have you got what it takes to become our Senior Account Officer?

• Experience of working within the Financial Sector with a minimum of 4 years' experience, ideally within Private Banking or with Independent Financial Advisors;
• You enjoy working in a challenging, fast paced environment and look for the opportunity to excel in all aspects of your role;
• Take personal pride in delivering high quality service to internal and external clients;
• Good communication skills: being able to build effective relationships and adapt communication style to the counterpart, always in a professional manner;
• Ability to listen to other opinions as well as being confident of your own and find balanced solutions;
• Be able and willing to look beyond the obvious and seek alternative solutions;
• Ability to work independently while keen to work as part of a team and assist colleagues;
• Willing to make the extra effort as required;
• Knowledge of Anti-Money Laundering regulations;
• Native-level Swedish speaker and fluency in English is a must, any other European language is an asset, particularly Norwegian.

As an equal opportunity employer, all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to gender, colour, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Given the sensitive nature of our business, industry sector and the role as described, the selected candidate is required to provide a criminal record (Bulletin n°3 for Luxembourgish residents). This excerpt will be kept by Utmost Luxembourg S.A. in compliance with article 8-5 (2) of the law of 23 July 2016 and for no longer than one month from the conclusion of the employment contract; otherwise, it will be destroyed without any undue delay should the candidate not be hired.

title: Group General Counsel - International Company (m/f)
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

Group General Counsel

Reporting line: Chief Executive Officer, with dotted reporting line to the Board.
Contract: permanent, full-time (40 hours per week). Location: Luxembourg, hybrid, with regular international travel.

1 The business and the role

The company operates an international online subscription and creator platform, with exposure to adult content, and which operates across the United Kingdom, the European Union and the US. The Group General Counsel is the most senior legal officer of the group.

2 Main responsibilities

1. Legal function leadership and Board support

• Build, staff and lead the group legal function, including recruitment, budget, external counsel panel and legal operations.
• Act as principal legal adviser to the Board, the founders and the executive team, and attend Board and committee meetings.
• Set and own the group's legal risk appetite, escalation framework and legal reporting to the Board and to investors.
• Manage disputes and litigation across jurisdictions, including instruction and supervision of external counsel.

2. Corporate, M&A and governance

• Lead corporate and M&A transactions end to end, including target assessment, due diligence, transaction documentation, signing, closing and PMI.
• Support fundraising rounds, investor documentation, shareholder arrangements and cap table matters.
• Own corporate governance across a multi-jurisdictional holding structure, including entity management, board and shareholder resolutions, statutory filings, registers of beneficial owners, delegated authority frameworks and group policies.
• Act as secretary to the Board and to group entity boards, or supervise that function.
• Coordinate with finance and tax on group structuring, intragroup agreements, transfer pricing documentation and substance requirements.

3. Data protection, artificial intelligence and digital regulation

• Own the group's data protection compliance programme under the EU GDPR and the UK GDPR, including records of processing, transfer mechanisms, data protection impact assessments, data subject rights, breach response and supervisory authority engagement.
• Advise on US privacy legislation applicable to the group's user base, including state level comprehensive privacy laws and applicable wiretapping and tracking technology claims.
• Own the group's artificial intelligence governance framework, including the classification of AI systems, transparency obligations for synthetic and AI generated content, model and vendor due diligence, training data and intellectual property questions, and readiness for the EU AI Act.
• Advise on the EU Digital Services Act and the UK Online Safety Act, including notice and action mechanisms, trusted flaggers, transparency reporting, risk assessment obligations, illegal content duties and children's access assessments.
• Advise on the EU Digital Markets Act, the audiovisual media services framework and platform to business regulation as applicable to the group's distribution channels.

4. High risk industry, trust and safety, and content compliance

• Advise on the legal and regulatory framework applicable to adult oriented and creator monetization platforms, including age assurance and identity verification, performer consent and record keeping obligations, nonconsensual intimate image takedown, CSAM prevention and reporting, and content moderation and appeals.
• Design and maintain creator terms, model releases, content licences, revenue share arrangements and agency and management arrangements.
• Advise on advertising, affiliate and performance marketing arrangements, influencer marketing rules and consumer protection requirements in the EU, the UK and the US.
• Manage intellectual property, including trademarks, copyright enforcement and anti-piracy programmes.

5. Payments, financial crime and sanctions

• Own the legal side of the group's payments stack, including acquirer and payment service provider agreements, alternative payment methods, payout and creator disbursement arrangements and merchant of record structures.
• Advise on card scheme rules as they apply to high risk and adult merchant categories, including high brand risk and integrity risk registration programmes, prohibited content rules, chargeback thresholds and remediation plans.
• Advise on PSD2 and strong customer authentication, electronic money and payment institution perimeter questions, and the implications of the EU instant payments and payment services reform.
• Own the group's KYC, AML, CTF and sanctions framework, including creator onboarding, transaction monitoring, and screening against EU, UK, US OFAC and other relevant measures.

6. Commercial and employment

• Negotiate the group's material commercial agreements, including technology, content, distribution, partnership and vendor agreements.
• Support the people function on employment law across multiple jurisdictions, including contracts, contractor classification, incentive schemes and internal investigations.

• Law degree from an EU or EEA or UK university.
• Admission in good standing to the bar of an EU or EEA Member State or UK.
• A minimum of 20 years of PQE legal experience, of which at least 10 years in a senior in house legal leadership role (General Counsel, Head of Legal or equivalent).
• Demonstrable experience of building and leading an international in house legal team across diverse jurisdictions.
• A track record of leading cross border M&A transactions in the US, UK and/or EU jurisdictions.
• Corporate governance experience in complex international structures.
• Recognised privacy certification (IAPP CIPP/E or equivalent) and hands on ownership of a GDPR compliance programme.
• Direct working knowledge of the EU/UK digital regulatory framework, including DSA, DMA, OSA, the AI Act, AVMS.
• Substantive experience in high risk regulated industries, and specifically in adult entertainment or creator platform compliance.
• Substantive experience of payment processing and billing for high-risk merchant categories.
• Experience in entertainment and media.
• Tax, KYC/AML and sanctions experience in a regulated or high risk environment.
• Experience advising founders, C level executives and Boards in a venture backed, high growth environment.
• English at level C (native/bilingual/proficient user).

title: Solution Architect I - Subsidy Projects (fixed-term 24 months) (m/f)
description:
Description des tâches:


Who we are

Luxembourg National Data Service (LNDS) is a brand of PNED G.I.E. an organisation created by the Luxembourg Government, to implement Luxembourg's strategies in research, innovation, and digitalisation.
LNDS enables value creation from secondary use of data, for public and private partners and supports the sharing and re-use of public sector data, in a trustable manner.
The LNDS service portfolio includes know-how, capabilities, tools, infrastructure, and data services.
Through efficient & responsible use of data and improving the secondary use of data, LNDS will support the acceleration of economic, ecological, and societal transitions.
www.lnds.lu | LNDS on LinkedIn


Purpose of the job / project

Help design and deliver the data infrastructure that Luxembourg and its European partners rely on for secure, lawful access to sensitive data. You will work alongside senior architects on real systems with real deadlines and take on your own architectural scope as you go.

This is a fixed-term position of 24 months, created to meet a sustained increase in architecture work across our EU project portfolio.
You will work on one or more projects from that portfolio — currently including STORE-1PLUSMG, USE-1PLUSMG, SCAILED, the European Compliance Stack, DDSSC2, COOPAIFA and PANDAI — with assignments set by portfolio priorities and evolving as projects start and close.
We are looking for a Solution Architect to help design and deliver secure, large-scale data infrastructure, working alongside our senior architects.
You will consolidate functional and non-functional requirements from data providers and partner organisations and translate them into architecture documentation.
You will contribute to the specification, configuration, integration, and technical validation of the components behind our data services.
Working with community frameworks such as Gaia-X, IDSA and DSSC, you will help build the data solutions our partners across Europe depend on.


What you will do

Architecture design and documentation

Learn and deliver the core architecture artefacts, starting from established LNDS patterns and templates, and taking on more of the design work as your experience grows.
Maintain the architecture documentation set across assigned projects — keeping it current, internally consistent and ready for formal review. Several projects require successive versioned releases approved at fixed milestones.

Requirements and analysis

Support senior architects in gathering and documenting functional and non-functional requirements from data providers, partner organisations and internal stakeholders.
Analyse and document business constraints.

Implementation support

Work with engineering and operations colleagues to turn architecture into working systems.
Support the specification, configuration, and integration of components.
Support technical validation and acceptance activities, including preparing test scenarios and evidence.

Standards, compliance and quality

Learn, adopt and apply LNDS architectural standards, patterns and review practices consistently, and flag where they do not fit.
Support the implementation of technical and organisational measures under Data Protection by Design and Default, working with Legal and data governance colleagues.

Project and consortium contribution

Contribute to project deliverables and milestones, tracking your own commitments and raising slippage early.
Support proposal preparation with technical input and effort estimation.


Who you are

BSc or MSc in a scientific, technological or engineering discipline related to computer science, information technology or computing.
1-2 years working explicitly as a solution or enterprise architect on large-scale or federated data systems.
Working knowledge of distributed systems, APIs and integration patterns, databases, and data modelling.
Exposure with cloud or container platforms, infrastructure-as-code, and CI/CD pipelines.
Foundational understanding of information security, authentication and authorisation, encryption, and network segmentation.
Able to write clear technical documentation and produce readable diagrams.
Awareness of GDPR and the broader EU data regulatory landscape.
Familiarity with agile delivery practices.
Excellent communication skills in English.
Working knowledge of one of Luxembourg's official languages (French, German or Luxembourgish) is a plus.
Curious, methodical, and comfortable speaking when you do not understand something.
Willingness to learn architectural concepts and methods, and to develop your information security and regulatory knowledge seriously.
Collaborative, adaptable, and able to work effectively in a cross-functional and multicultural environment.
Interest in health data, genomics, data spaces or public sector data infrastructure.
Prior experience in EU-funded projects is a plus.

description:
Description des tâches:


Who we are

Luxembourg National Data Service (LNDS) is a brand of PNED G.I.E. an organisation created by the Luxembourg Government, to implement Luxembourg's strategies in research, innovation, and digitalisation. Purpose of the job / project

Help design the data infrastructure that Luxembourg and its European partners rely on for secure, lawful access to sensitive data. The specifications you write will be implemented by organisations across Europe. This is a fixed-term position of 24 months, created to meet a sustained increase in architecture work across our EU project portfolio.
You will work on one or more projects from that portfolio — currently including STORE-1PLUSMG, USE-1PLUSMG, SCAILED, the European Compliance Stack, DSSC2, COOPAIFA and PANDAI — with assignments set by portfolio priorities and evolving as projects start and close.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Solution Architect to lead the design and specification of large-scale federated data infrastructure, with a particular emphasis on data spaces.
You will lead the design of solution architectures end to end, from requirements through to delivery support. You will contribute to and produce reference architectures, blueprints and interoperability profiles to support implementation by partner organisations across Europe. You will lead work packages where LNDS holds that responsibility and represent us in multi-partner consortia. Working with community frameworks such as Gaia-X, IDSA and DSSC.


What you will do

Solution design and architecture

Design and own end-to-end solution architectures for assigned projects, covering system context, component and interface definition, data flows, storage strategy, protocols and tooling.
Define non-functional requirements with the same rigor as functional ones: security, interoperability, scalability, availability, accountability, and auditability.
Establish and maintain technical and organizational measures frameworks under Data Protection by Design and Default.

Specification, procurement and conformance

Gather and consolidate functional and non-functional requirements from data providers, partner organisations and internal stakeholders.
Analyse and document business constraints.
Build reference architectures, blueprints and interoperability profiles that other organisations can implement without further interpretation.

Work package and task leadership in EU projects

Represent LNDS in consortium technical discussions and contribute to achieving consensus among partners with different technical perspectives.
Contribute architectural input to proposals for new calls, including effort estimation and work package design.

Technical leadership and mentoring

Provide technical direction to development and operations teams implementing your designs and stay engaged through delivery rather than handing over a document.
The role offers the opportunity to mentor junior architects: reviewing their artefacts, bringing them into consortium work, and helping them grow towards specification and framework of responsibility. An appetite for this is welcome, though it is not a requirement for the position.

Stakeholder engagement

Engage stakeholders at national and European level: data providers, ministries, hospitals, research institutions, national authorities and consortium partners across the EU to elicit requirements and translate them into technical specifications that hold across organisations and jurisdictions.
Explain architectural decisions and their consequences to non-technical stakeholders, including where a requirement cannot be met as stated and what the alternatives cost.

Regulatory alignment and risk:

Apply Data Protection by Design and Default throughout the architecture. Ensure architectural designs appropriately address applicable regulatory and compliance requirements.
Identify architectural and technical risks early, quantify their impact, and propose mitigations that project boards can act on.


Who you are

BSc or MSc in a scientific, technological or engineering discipline related to computer science, information technology or computing.
5 to 10 years working explicitly as a solution or enterprise architect on large-scale or federated data systems.
Experience with distributed and federated architectures, APIs, cloud and container platforms, and infrastructure as-code.
Understanding information security: authentication and authorisation, encryption, network segmentation, and how it shapes architectural decisions.
Experience with TOGAF, ArchiMate or another enterprise architecture framework, and the discipline to keep artefacts current.
Familiarity with agile delivery, particularly product and service ownership and Scrum.
Able to move between several projects with competing demands and prioritise without dropping commitments.
Collaborative and adaptable, and effective in a cross-functional and multicultural environment.
Working knowledge of EU and LU data regulations such as GDPR, DGA, EHDS, the Data Act, the AI Act and NIS2 is a plus.
Direct experience implementing or contributing to a data space framework (Gaia-X, IDSA, DSSC Blueprint) is a plus.
Experience in EU-funded projects: work package or task leadership, deliverable ownership, consortium working is an advantage.
Excellent communication skills in English. Working knowledge of one of Luxembourg's official languages (French, German or Luxembourgish) is a plus.
